summary.name: tty7
summary.one_liner: tty7 is a terminal workbench whose background server keeps shells and coding agents running across app quits, reboots, and laptop switches.
keywords: keep shells running after closing window
use_cases: keep builds running after closing the terminal window
monitor multiple coding agents and get notified when one needs input
manage remote servers over SSH with profiles and SFTP
review git branches and diffs alongside the terminal
script terminal panes from other tools or agents
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a terminal app with a background server that owns the shells, so sessions survive closing the app or rebooting. It adds shell input features such as history-based ghost suggestions, flag-aware tab completion, syntax highlighting, and multi-line editing. It has a native Rust SSH stack with profiles, SFTP, and port forwarding, plus remote workspaces. It shows git branch and diff counts, a source control panel, GitHub issues and pull requests, and a bundled CLI for scripting panes and reading screens. It recognises 28 coding CLIs by command and shows per-pane status for them without wrapping them.
notable: Background server keeps shells alive without tmux
Recognises 28 coding agent CLIs and notifies when one needs input
Native Rust SSH stack with SFTP and port forwarding
Bundled tty7 CLI for driving panes from scripts
caveats: Performance figures are vendor benchmarks on a single Apple M1 Pro setup
Page does not state a license name beyond 'free and open source'
